Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of 
${\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$

If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then

${\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-5,-3),$ the arc of the quarter-circle for $x\in (-3,-1),$ and the line segment for $x\in [-1,4].$ Using the additive property of integrals, we write

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-3).$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh \\  & =2\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis,

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-4.
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-3,-1).$ The corresponding region is a combination of an inverted quarter-circle of radius $2$ and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh-\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =2\cdot 2-\frac{1}{4}\pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =4-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis,

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=\pi -4.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,4].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)\cdot 5 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =-4+\pi -4+10 \\  & =2+\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
